posts.author: Dutchelm05
posts.content_md:
While in my sanctuary, away from the kids, I was able to read a little.

This section caught my interest.

It is from Saxby Pratical Holographry Pg 123 (hope he's not mad for violating and copyrights)

Has anyone tried this set up?

I thought it a pretty clean and easy set up to do a modified Denisyuk while being able to adjust the beam ratio. Also retain the stability of the single beam set up.

The ND filter can be tilted until to adjust the object light.

The down side is the object has to be on its side.

Any comments?

I know this is not neccessarily and DCG question, but should work well for DCG.

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md: I have tried it in the past and it does work. The downside is that the object has to be rather far from the plate for it to catch the bypassed light. There is a better way to do it with mirrors. I remember there was a Norwegian holographer who had a website with photo's of this setup, but I don't remember the address.

posts.author: dave battin
posts.content_md: Sorry for getting side tracked there, yes Tony i tried Saxby’s by-pass setup many years back. it works well, you will need to use a good ND filter, if you have gel type filters you may want to cement it between two microscope slides, if not your filter may show nasty signs of the dreaded "wood graining effect" ........

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
One spatial filter, BS stated in drawing was actaully a ND filter when I did this geometry.

[http://www.holograms3d.com/Illustration ... erence.jpg](http://www.holograms3d.com/Illustrations/H2SetUpCoherence.jpg)

But I actually did this as the coherence length of my laser is so long.

[http://www.holograms3d.com/Illustrations/H2SetUp.jpg](http://www.holograms3d.com/Illustrations/H2SetUp.jpg)

Here is how I did the elephant. Not exactly what you're asking but I wanted to illlustrate how I used non standard configurations to keep stability in check. By ever so slightly tweaking the single spatial filter I could adjust the beam ratios of the H1 and H2 beams. Move the beam just a little up and more light goes to H2 and less to H1. I did this in the two previous set ups also. The simple way, and you can observe this, is to slightly move the mirror directly before the spatial filter. This allowed me to move the light while keeping the spatial filter in allignment.

[http://www.holograms3d.com/Illustrations/H2SetUp.jpg](http://www.holograms3d.com/Illustrations/H2SetUp.jpg)
